items.name: Complete writer inventory for data/character-*/ai-config/tts-config.json
evidence: grep -rn 'tts-config.json' over *.js/*.mjs/*.py/*.sh: the ONLY code that writes the per-character file is services/aiConfigStore.js:34-38 writeJson() via mergeJson() (aiConfigStore.js:57), reached only from saveTTSConfig() (aiConfigStore.js:185-188).
grep -rn 'saveTTSConfig': exactly ONE caller in the whole repo — routes/api/elevenLabsApiRoutes.js:477 (POST /api/elevenlabs/tts/config). No service, boot path, script, or Python wrapper writes it.

routes/aiSettingsRoutes.js:134-142 READS the dir only (readJsonIfExists). services/aiPromptGeneratorService.js:357 READS agent_id only. routes/api/elevenLabsApiRoutes.js:339 (/tts/generate) resolves config read-only.

install.sh:405-419 writes the ROOT-LEVEL data/ai-config/tts-config.json (eleven_v3 / voice_id ""), never data/character-N/. That stray dir does not exist on Orlok today (`ls data/ai-config` -> No such file).

getAIConfigDir() (aiConfigStore.js:9-14) resolves cfg.dataPath, i.e. data/character-<selectedCharacter> — so every write lands on whichever character is SELECTED at write time, not on a character named in the request.
items.remaining_work: None for the inventory itself — it is now proven, not assumed. Record it so no future session re-hunts phantom writers in boot paths or Python.

items.name: Second clobberer IDENTIFIED: an interactive Save on /ai-settings/tts (not a test suite)
evidence: git show e00aa2f2 -- data/character-3/ai-config/tts-config.json captures the drifted file verbatim: model eleven_v3->eleven_flash_v2_5, stability 0.25->0.6, similarity_boost 0.6->0.4, and three NEW keys style:0.8, use_speaker_boost:true, conversationalMode:false. voice_id and speed survived (the v9.2.0 merge fix worked).

The drifted blob ends '\\ No newline at end of file' — the exact signature of writeJson()'s JSON.stringify(data,null,2) in services/aiConfigStore.js:36. A hand edit or an agent Write would normally carry a trailing newline. This proves an IN-APP write through POST /api/elevenlabs/tts/config.

The key set is byte-for-byte the payload public/js/ai-settings-tts.js:474-503 builds: it always sends model+stability+similarity_boost+conversationalMode, and sends style+use_speaker_boost ONLY when model !== 'eleven_v3' (line 497-503). The drifted file has model=flash AND style — no other code in the repo constructs that shape.

Every drifted value is a valid step-0.1 slider position (0.6 / 0.4 / 0.8) and the model is a literal <option> in views/ai-settings/tts.ejs:74 — i.e. someone/something set the form and clicked 'Save Configuration'.

NOT the test suites: no browser spec clicks a TTS save. tests/browser/ai-settings.spec.js:214 only asserts the button is visible; tests/browser/actual-usage-testing.spec.js:1410-1436 only counts sliders and screenshots. tests/system/ai-audio.test.js:192 posts 0.5/0.5/eleven_v3 (different values) and now restores.

Independent second occurrence of the same mechanism on a DIFFERENT character: git show 193ad77f -- data/character-2/ai-config/tts-config.json shows Mina's file gaining conversationalMode/style/use_speaker_boost with the same no-trailing-newline signature during a browser-suite window on 2026-08-19, and that drift was then COMMITTED as canonical.
items.remaining_work: The mechanism is proven; the ACTOR (Aaron experimenting vs a prior agent driving the page via Playwright/MCP) is not, and does not need to be. Fix the path, not the actor: (a) act on the operator's standing decision in docs/handoff/2026-08-19-v104-overnight.md — model/stability/similarity/style/speaker-boost are dead on the conversational path (agent overrides all false) and eleven_v3 ignores style+speed, so REMOVE the dead controls and leave voice selection + a deep link to elevenlabs.io; (b) if any control stays, make POST /tts/config reject a body that changes model/stability/similarity_boost without an explicit intent flag, and log every accepted change with the before/after at warn level so /var/log/monsterbox.err names the next clobber; (c) require the request to name the characterId instead of silently targeting selectedCharacter.

items.name: ai-audio.test.js snapshot/restore is fixed but the restore itself re-materializes defaults and can null a voice
evidence: tests/system/ai-audio.test.js:192-232 — the 2026-08-17 fix (snapshot in `before`, restore in `finally`) is present and correct in intent.

The snapshot is the GET response, and GET is getTTSConfig() (services/aiConfigStore.js:152-183), which MATERIALIZES defaults: conversationalMode:false, style:0.0, use_speaker_boost:true, speed clamped. Posting that back through mergeJson persists keys the file never had — exactly the three keys Mina's file gained on 2026-08-19 (193ad77f).

Worse case: getTTSConfig() returns voice_id:null when none is configured (aiConfigStore.js:156, 175). mergeJson (aiConfigStore.js:57-63) only skips `undefined`, so a restore would WRITE "voice_id": null — which then fails config/schemas/tts-config.schema.json (voice_id must be a string) and breaks the gate, or silently erases identity.

tests/system/ai-audio.test.js:138 BASE_URL defaults to http://localhost:3000, which is HTTPS-only in production — so on a prod node the fetch throws and the whole block no-ops; with BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 it hits the live app and writes real files.
items.remaining_work: Snapshot the FILE (raw bytes) rather than the GET response and restore the bytes; or make mergeJson refuse a null/empty voice_id outright (it should never be possible to null an identity field through a merge). Either fix is small and testable in tests/unit/ai-config-store.test.js.

items.name: The gate cannot catch tuning drift — only voice_id is guarded
evidence: tests/unit/tts-voice-identity.test.js asserts voice_id matches disk, no two characters share a voice, unconfigured characters throw, and speed is within 0.7-1.2. It never compares stability / similarity_boost / model / speed to any canonical.
config/schemas/tts-config.schema.json requires only `model` (any string) and types the rest — no enum, no canonical pinning, and `speed` is not even declared.
So the 2026-08-20 drift (0.6 / 0.4 / eleven_flash_v2_5) would have passed `npm run gate` cleanly.

scripts/log-review.mjs:97-114 IS a real detector — it diffs voice_id/stability/similarity_boost/speed/model against `git show HEAD:<path>` and raises an ERROR. That is what caught the 2026-08-20 drift (commit 5f4d94a8).

But it compares against git HEAD, so once a drifted value is COMMITTED the detector goes blind — which is precisely what happened to Mina in 193ad77f, where a service-written state got folded into canonical and the drift became the baseline.
items.remaining_work: Add a unit assertion that every character's stability/similarity_boost/speed/voice_id match the committed agent snapshot in config/elevenlabs/agents/ (one source of truth, gate-enforced, shrink-only if a deliberate divergence is needed). Change log-review to compare against the SNAPSHOT as well as git HEAD so committing a drift no longer silences it.

items.name: Split of voice claims: provable statically now vs needs a live ear-check
evidence: PROVABLE NOW (done or doable without hardware): the complete writer inventory; the clobber mechanism (e00aa2f2 diff + no-trailing-newline signature + client payload shape); local-vs-snapshot tuning drift for all six characters; snapshot-vs-live staleness (Mina proven); Mina's singing instruction; whisper tags present; Dragomir's voice id and its library name; the agent-side tts override lockout; optimize_streaming_latency = 0 live.

NEEDS AN EAR-CHECK (defer to implementation, per CLAUDE.md 'Audio claims are proven by ear-check, never by API success'): that each node PLAYS its designed voice (recorded + transcribed, voiceUsed compared to canonical, as scripts/fleet-audio/results/earcheck-2026-08-16T09-49-47.json did when it caught Dragomir's retired voice); whether Mina audibly carries a Romanian accent (a property of voice hkk1bPcdsxSQCLzLFMT2, not of any config field); whether whisper is audible rather than merely tagged; whether the corrected tuning is perceptibly better.

Ear-check tooling caveat (CLAUDE.md + docs/handoff/2026-08-19-v104-overnight.md): `npm run earcheck` scores a node it cannot SSH into as OFFLINE even while it serves fine — run it from Orlok and confirm any OFFLINE with `curl -sk https://<peer>:3000/health`. It also never reads the speaker-mute flag, so a muted node scores identically to a broken one.
Mina is hardware-unstable (docs/handoff/2026-08-20-recovery-realignment.md:35-41) — drive her ear-check FROM Orlok and treat her as a deploy target, not a session host.
items.remaining_work: Sequence the ear-checks AFTER the static fixes land and after the fleet is powered — nothing acoustic is claimable before then. Consider teaching earcheck.mjs to read the mute flag so a muted node stops reading as a dead one.

dependencies_on_other_streams: Ear-check items depend on the fleet being powered and on Mina's USB/audio hardware being stable (recovery-realignment §Mina is hardware-unstable). Static work has no hardware dependency.

The 'remove dead TTS controls' fix overlaps the ghost-settings / dashboard-freshness stream — both edit views/ai-settings/* and public/js/ai-settings-*.js. Coordinate so one stream owns the AI-settings pages.
The canonical-STT stream shares services/aiConfigStore.js (saveSTTConfig/getSTTConfig) and the same POST-merge semantics; the same clobber shape can hit stt-config.json.
The deploy pre-flight check touches scripts/deploy-to-animatronic.sh, shared with the fleet/deploy stream.
will_conflict_with: Any stream editing public/js/ai-settings-tts.js or views/ai-settings/tts.ejs (dashboard/ghost-settings cleanup).
Any stream editing scripts/log-review.mjs or docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md (log-review runs continuously per the mega-session plan and rewrites that tracker).
open_questions: Does Aaron want the TTS tuning controls REMOVED outright (his standing decision on dead controls) or kept read-only with a deep link to elevenlabs.io? Removal makes the clobber structurally impossible and is the smaller long-term surface.

Is the local/agent split still wanted at all? Nothing in tts-config.json can reach a conversation (all tts overrides are false at the agent), so the local values only bite the one-shot say/scene path — the two may deserve explicitly different tunings rather than being forced to agree.
Mina's `ro` language_preset with a Romanian first_message: delete it, or keep it as an unused capability? overrides.agent.language is TRUE, so it is one client field away from being reachable.

Who actually clicked Save on 2026-08-20 — Aaron or a prior agent driving the page? Not needed for the fix, but if it was an agent, the same agent class may click other Save buttons on other settings pages.
fleet_wide_notes: Every finding here was taken on the Orlok node (192.168.8.120) against the working tree at HEAD 609245f5 plus the uncommitted node-local state; no file was modified and no hardware or audio was driven. Two live ElevenLabs MCP reads were performed (agents_list, agents_get for Mina, creative_list_voices) — both read-only. The single most useful artifact for the implementation session is commit e00aa2f2, the rescue snapshot of Orlok's working tree taken at 22:12 on 2026-08-20, fourteen minutes BEFORE the canonical restore: it preserves the drifted tts-config byte-for-byte and is what turned an unidentified writer into a proven one.
